title: Type-mismatch list silently truncated to 10 with no "... and N more" indicator (inconsistent with the missing-features block)
description: _format_feature_mismatch renders the missing-feature block with an explicit overflow line (`if n_missing > 20: lines.append(f'  ... and {n_missing - 20} more')`, lines 179-180) but the type-mismatch block iterates `type_mismatches[:10]` (line 185) with NO equivalent overflow notice. When a wide model is scored with more than 10 declared-categorical columns each supplied as a numeric dtype, the operator is told to 'fix the upstream schema or re-train' but the diagnostic shows only the first 10 offending columns and gives no signal that further columns are also mis-typed. The truncation is real: the type-mismatch raise (lines 256-267) fires precisely when `usable` is non-empty and nothing is missing, i.e. all expected features are present but >=1 categorical was passed numeric — a wide model can easily exceed 10 such columns. The result is a fail-loud error whose remediation guidance is silently incomplete, so the operator may fix the 10 shown columns, re-run, and hit the same error again on the next 10.
evidence: Lines 175-187: missing block has `for name in missing[:20]: ...` followed by `if n_missing > 20: lines.append(f'  ... and {n_missing - 20} more')`. Type block (183-187): `lines.append('Type mismatch(es):'); for col, expected_type, actual_type in type_mismatches[:10]: lines.append(...)` then `lines.append('')` — no `if len(type_mismatches) > 10` overflow line. `n_missing` is computed (line 167) but there is no `n_type_mismatches`. The header count uses `n_expected`/`n_available` only, so the total type-mismatch count is never surfaced anywhere in the message.
